paragraphs.heading: What an eruption is
paragraphs.text: In a volcanic eruption, material is expelled from a vent or fissure of a volcano. Volcanologists have picked out several types of eruption. Many are named after famous volcanoes where that kind of behavior has been seen. Some volcanoes show a single characteristic type during a period of activity, while others run through a whole sequence of types in one eruptive series.

paragraphs.heading: Three main types
paragraphs.text: There are three main types of eruption. In a magmatic eruption, gas inside the magma decompresses and drives the magma forward. A phreatic eruption is driven by steam that is superheated because magma is close by. It releases no magma, and instead breaks existing rock into grains. A phreatomagmatic eruption is driven by magma and water interacting directly.

paragraphs.heading: Explosive and effusive
paragraphs.text: Eruptions can also be sorted by their activity into explosive and effusive ones. Explosive eruptions are marked by gas-driven explosions that throw out magma and tephra. Effusive eruptions pour out lava with no significant explosion. At one extreme are effusive Hawaiian eruptions, with their lava fountains and runny lava flows, and these are typically not very dangerous. At the other extreme are Plinian eruptions, which are large, violent and highly dangerous explosive events.

paragraphs.heading: A ladder of strength
paragraphs.text: Within the broad types there are several subtypes, and they can be ranked. The weakest are Hawaiian and submarine eruptions, then Strombolian, then Vulcanian and Surtseyan. Stronger still are Pelean eruptions, followed by Plinian ones, and the strongest of all are called ultra-Plinian. Two kinds, subglacial and phreatic, are defined by the mechanism that drives them, and their strength varies.

paragraphs.heading: Measuring strength
paragraphs.text: The volcanic explosivity index, or VEI for short, is a scale that runs from 0 to 8 and measures how strong an eruption is. It works much like the Richter scale used for earthquakes: each step up in value stands for a tenfold increase in magnitude. The vast majority of eruptions have a VEI between 0 and 2. The index does not capture every property of an eruption that may be seen as important.

paragraphs.heading: A Hawaiian eruption up close
paragraphs.text: Hawaiian eruptions take their name from the Hawaiian volcanoes, such as Mauna Loa. They are calm events in which very fluid basalt-type lava with a low gas content pours out. They often start with a row of vent eruptions strung along a fissure vent, known as a curtain of fire. They fade once the lava starts to concentrate at a few of the vents. Eruptions of this kind often last an extremely long time. Puʻu ʻŌʻō, a volcanic cone on Kilauea, erupted without a break for more than 35 years.

paragraphs.heading: No fixed style
paragraphs.text: A volcano is not tied to one eruptive style. Volcanoes often show many different types, passive and explosive alike, even within a single eruptive cycle. They also do not always erupt straight up from one crater near the peak. Some have lateral and fissure eruptions, and many Hawaiian eruptions start from rift zones.
